title: Morning Headlines
intro: An active US-Iran war edges toward a deal, a school massacre shocks Thailand, history is made in vaccine science, Houthi forces escalate in Yemen, and rattled markets round out a consequential Friday.

items.title: US-Iran War: Hormuz Deal 'Edging Closer' as Trump Says Conflict Will End 'Pretty Soon'
items.subtitle: Al Jazeera / CNN
items.summary: Oman-brokered talks aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping are advancing, with draft texts circulating between Tehran and Washington, even as Iran publicly denies direct negotiations. A deal would lift a stranglehold on global oil flows that has driven energy prices sharply higher since the war began in late February 2026.

items.title: Seven Killed in School Shooting at Debsirin Nonthaburi School Near Bangkok
items.subtitle: CNN / Bangkok Post / NPR
items.summary: A student opened fire at the 3,000-pupil Debsirin Nonthaburi School north of Bangkok, killing three teachers and three students and wounding 15 others before dying from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The attack is one of Thailand's deadliest school shootings and has prompted calls for urgent action on gun control in the country.

items.title: FDA Approves Moderna's mFLUSIVA — the First mRNA Flu Vaccine in US History
items.subtitle: NBC News / STAT News / TIME
items.summary: The FDA cleared Moderna's mRNA-1010 influenza vaccine for adults 50 and older, extending the mRNA platform — proven during COVID-19 — to annual flu shots for the first time; it was 27% more effective than standard flu vaccines in trials. The technology also allows far faster production, a critical advantage for matching emerging strains or responding to a new pandemic.

items.title: Houthis Launch Large-Scale Drone and Missile Assault on Saudi-Backed Forces in Yemen
items.subtitle: Bloomberg / Al Jazeera / South China Morning Post
items.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis struck government-held positions with ballistic missiles and drones on Thursday, killing at least 30–58 Saudi-aligned troops in one of the single deadliest Houthi attacks in four years. Eleven civilians were separately wounded in strikes on Saudi territory, drawing a sharp warning from Riyadh of further escalation.

items.title: Global Markets Retreat as Iran-War Tensions Lift Oil and Fed Official Warns Inflation Still Too High
items.subtitle: Bloomberg Markets
items.summary: US equity futures slipped and oil jumped on renewed geopolitical jitters tied to the Iran war, reviving inflation concerns ahead of Friday's closely watched July jobs report. A Federal Reserve official added to the caution, saying inflation remains well above target and that monetary policy must continue to impose meaningful restraint.
